title: Coefficient-domain and exact common-stage realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$. Pullback, tensor and both direct images restrict to the displayed categories. Internal Hom restricts to $\mathcal C$ in both variables and has the evaluation-defined coefficient comparisons: for $n\ge m\ge1$ and $K,L\in\mathcal C_{X,A_n}$,
$$R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(K,L)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{A_m}(K\otimes^L A_m,L\otimes^L A_m),$$
and the corresponding formula holds from $R$ to $A_n$. Here the map is the transpose of scalar extension of evaluation. If $K,L$ have Tor intervals $[a,b],[c,e]$ and $\dim X\le d$ with $d\ge0$, the finite-stage Hom interval is $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$; the interval $[c-b,e-a]$ and the formula $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$ are asserted only for a site-perfect first argument, meaning locally a bounded complex of finite projective coefficient modules [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Integral pullback and tensor are completed operations. Their values and those of both direct images at field stages are the specified coefficient-passage values, with the rational internal Hom identification preserving evaluation.
For every finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset F$, scalar extension is exact triangulated. More generally, let $T,S$ be two such schemes. Any family of exact functors $\Phi_E:D^b_c(T,E)\to D^b_c(S,E)$, with natural scalar comparisons $T_{F/E}\Phi_E\simeq\Phi_F T_{F/E}$ satisfying the identity, associator and shift equations, descends to an exact functor on the common-stage category. Scalar-compatible natural transformations and their equations descend as well. That common-stage category is idempotent-complete triangulated, and its finite-stage embeddings are exact.

proof.text: At each $A_n$, apply clauses (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] to the given $f$ and the finite-Tor inputs. These respectively restrict $Lf^*$, $\otimes^L$, $Rf_*$, and $Rf_!$ to the displayed finite-stage categories. Its hypotheses are exactly separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type schemes over the fixed $k$, with $\ell\ne p$; they hold here for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Opening sentence, proved constructible domains; stability clauses (i)–(iv)

proof.text: For $K,L\in\mathcal C_{X,A_n}$, [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] gives bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(K,L)$, on the small pro-etale site used by the operation datum. With input intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,e]$ and any integer $d\ge0$ satisfying $\dim X\le d$, its stated interval is precisely $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$. This proves the general finite-stage Hom restriction and the asserted dimension-dependent bound.

Apply [thm-coef-finite-hom] with $A=A_n$, $B=A_m$ and $M=L$. The hypotheses $n\ge m\ge1$ and $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ are those of the item. The resulting isomorphism is exactly the displayed finite coefficient comparison. The theorem characterizes its arrow as the unique tensor–Hom transpose of scalar extension of evaluation; thus the comparison here is that specified arrow, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism.

When the first input $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ is site-perfect in the sense of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], it is locally on the small pro-etale site a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $(A_n)_X$-modules, i.e. perfect in the sense of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] for the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_n)_X)$. That lemma gives the canonical evaluation isomorphism $K^\vee\otimes^L_{A_n}L\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(K,L)$ with $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(K,(A_n)_X)$, for every $L$. Clause (ii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] gives, under exactly this extra hypothesis, the sharper Tor interval $[c-b,e-a]$. No application of either result to a merely constructible finite-Tor first input is made; that case was covered instead by step 2 (and the origin of $\mathbf A^1$ in clause (ii) shows the sharper bound fails without site-perfectness).

source.place: Opening domains and site-perfect qualification in prop-functor-package; stability clause (ii)

proof.text: At $R$, [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] restricts the completed pullback and completed tensor to the derived-complete integral constructible categories, with their stated finite reductions. Apply [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to obtain the same restriction for the specified $Rf_*$. Apply [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] to the specified compactification reduction tower defining $Rf_!$. That theorem applies to its derived limit with exactly the quotient/restriction-of-scalars transitions, and proves completeness and one finite cohomological interval for all its reductions. All three results allow our finite-type $k$-schemes with $\ell$ invertible; the compact-support result requires the separated finite-type $f$ assumed here. These are preservation theorems for the actual completed operations, so the definition of the integral category alone is not being used to assert preservation.

source.place: Opening integral preservation; completed pullback/tensor and the two direct images

proof.text: For integral $K,L$, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supplies uniform finite-level Tor intervals from the bounded residue reductions; it does not assert site-perfectness. Now [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] applies to all $K,L\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and places their ambient internal Hom in that same category. Its canonical evaluation-defined reduction comparison gives the required formula from $R$ to every $A_n$. Consequently this step uses neither a site-perfect model for arbitrary constructible objects nor an inference of completeness from levelwise boundedness alone.

Use the raw rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the finite-representative common-stage construction of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. By [lem-fix-operation-reduction], the pullback, tensor, and two direct-image operations and their coefficient comparisons commute with rationalization and common-stage scalar extension. Thus their field values are the specified coefficient-passage values of the integral outputs established in step 5, and belong to the displayed field categories. The same result supplies scalar compatibility for internal Hom; [lem-coef-rational-operations] identifies the rationalized integral internal Hom with the field internal Hom and explicitly preserves evaluation, including under finite scalar extension. Applied to the integral outputs of step 6 and then to finite representatives, these identifications give internal-Hom restriction and the required evaluation identification at both field stages.

source.place: Opening field passage: lem-coef-rational-operations; basic operation coefficient passage

proof.text: For each finite inclusion $E\subset F$, apply [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated] with $L=F$ to $T$ (and to $S$ when needed). It states that this scalar-extension functor on the rationalized constructible categories preserves shifts and distinguished triangles. This is exactly the finite coefficient-field exactness asserted here.

The item's finite stages $D^b_c(-,E)$ and common-stage category $\mathcal C_T$ are those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], while [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] is stated for the stages of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and the pair category $\mathcal P_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Our separated finite-type $k$-schemes $T,S$ are noetherian, finite-dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible, so [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] gives exact equivalences $J_{W,E}$ ($W=T,S$), the identity on the common integral objects and on localized Hom groups, with scalar comparisons $j_{W,F/E}:J_{W,F}T^{\mathrm{sf}}_{F/E}\simeq T^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{F/E}J_{W,E}$ respecting identities, shifts and the associators, and the induced exact equivalences $J_W:\mathcal C_W\simeq\mathcal P_W$ which identify finite-stage inclusions, shifts and distinguished triangles. Put $\Phi^{p}_E=J_{S,E}\Phi_EJ_{T,E}^{-1}$ and $\beta^p_{F/E}=(\Phi^p_F j_{T,F/E})\circ J_{S,F}(\beta_{F/E})\circ j_{S,F/E}^{-1}$, all at the transported object. Since the $j$ respect identities, associators and shifts, the identity, associator and shift equations assumed for $\beta$ give those of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] for $\beta^p$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to $(\Phi^p_E,\beta^p_{F/E})$: it gives an exact $\Phi^p:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$, represented on $u$ by $\beta^{p,-1}_{M/F}\circ\Phi^p_M(u)\circ\beta^p_{M/E}$, and descent of compatible transformations and their equations by the same formula. Then $\Phi=J_S^{-1}\Phi^pJ_T$ is an exact functor $\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal C_S$, as a composite of exact functors. Since $J_T,J_S$ conjugate common-stage arrows by the same $j$, these cancel, and $\Phi$ has value $(E,\Phi_EK)$ on $(E,K)$ and is represented on $u:T^{\mathrm{sf}}_{M/E}K\to T^{\mathrm{sf}}_{M/F}L$ by $\beta_{M/F}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ\beta_{M/E}$. Transformations and their equations transport the same way. This supplies all of the requested functor and transformation descent, with the given comparisons.

Apply [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] to $\mathcal P_T$: it is an idempotent-complete ordinary triangulated category, and every finite-stage embedding $j^{\mathrm{pbc}}_E:D^b_c(T,E)^{\mathrm{pbc}}\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact. By [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] (hypotheses checked in step 9), $J_T:\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal P_T$ is an exact equivalence, exact also in the reverse direction, preserving shifts and common-stage distinguished triangles in both directions and identifying the finite-stage inclusions: $J_Tj^{\mathrm{sf}}_E\cong j^{\mathrm{pbc}}_EJ_{T,E}$. Hence the triangulated category $\mathcal C_T$ is idempotent complete (an idempotent $e$ of $\mathcal C_T$ splits because $J_T(e)$ splits in $\mathcal P_T$ and $J_T$ is an equivalence), and $j^{\mathrm{sf}}_E\cong J_T^{-1}j^{\mathrm{pbc}}_EJ_{T,E}$ is a composite of exact functors, hence exact. These are properties of the literal common-stage category $\mathcal C_T$; no Karoubi envelope is inserted. Together with steps 8–9 this proves the remaining exact common-stage realization assertions.
